data.body:
Plan review 2026-11-16 (job 1794884083599153884) returned BLOCK. Two of the findings are design problems the plan cannot fix by editing, and I have verified both against the code paths the reviewer cites:
1. Mechanical (fixable): the streamed engine's ledger-anchor commit (mark :2) is rebuilt from the full boundary tree, so D lines on the checkpoint alone would be undone. Fix: apply the same D lines to :1 and :2.
2. Semantic (needs a decision): deleting folded .retired sources leaves each swept ticket's newest SNAPSHOT citing source uuids no longer on disk. fsck then reports SNAPSHOT_MISSING_SOURCES ("NOT auto-rebuildable, human triage required") for every swept ticket, and rebuild_source_state / rebuild_snapshot_from_full_log refuse to run on them (the b636 incomplete-log guard). Rebuild also builds authorship_ledger only from raw files on disk.
3. Semantic (needs a decision): non-reducer readers consume retired events directly: epic_bug_screen._first_in_progress_ns (retired STATUS), event_metrics revert counts via reduce_ticket(include_retired=True), and _distinct_file_impact_ticket (retired FILE_IMPACT). Exempting only CREATE changes their outputs; the reducer-equality test cannot detect that.
The sweep shrinks the CI-guarded blobless pack by about 0 (the 2026-08-29 re-scope), so it is secondary hygiene only. Not claimed. Paused for an operator decision, for example: teach fsck/rebuild that sources older than a reclaim checkpoint are legitimately absent and accept the metric changes; narrow the sweep to event types no reader consumes; or close this story as wontfix. 8dc4 (the dry run) does not depend on this story and proceeds without the sweep option.
